scenes.title: Your money. Your machine.
scenes.say: Most money apps want your logins, and your data on their servers. fire doesn't.

scenes.title: Private by default.
scenes.say: Everything lives in one JSON file on your own machine. Set a master key, and it's AES-256 encrypted at rest. fire is read-only, so it never moves a cent. And it's open source.

scenes.title: Locked down by default.
scenes.say: One command starts it behind HTTPS, with an API key, strict security headers and rate limits already on. No analytics, and no tracking.

scenes.title: Make it yours.
scenes.say: Every tab is a board of sections. Collapse, reorder, or pin any card to your dashboard.

scenes.title: Ask Claude about your money.
scenes.sub: 16 read-only MCP tools + the fire-coach skill
scenes.prompt: what happens if I lose my job?
scenes.after: You'd have **{runwayMonths} months** of runway at today's spending.
scenes.say: Connect Claude through sixteen read-only MCP tools, add the FIRE coach skill, and ask about your money in plain English.

scenes.title: Your data stays portable.
scenes.say: Export or restore everything as JSON or CSV, and every feature is also a REST endpoint.

scenes.title: Pocket-sized.
bullets: Self-host it, or try the live demo
scenes.say: It works from a wide monitor down to your phone.

scenes.title: Your money. Your machine.
scenes.say: fire is free and open source. Run it yourself, or try it live at lifefire dot netlify dot app.
